01

Setting specification

Task

Construct a rank-$k$ orthogonal right projection $P$ approximating the optimal rank-$k$ residual.

Admissible model

The matrix $A\in\mathbb{R}^{m\times n}$ is arbitrary real, with $d_{\mathrm{min}}=\min\{m,n\}$, $1\le k<d_{\mathrm{min}}$, and $1\le p\le\infty$. No rank, singular-gap, or spectral-decay promise is imposed.

Oracle interface

The information $m,n,k,p,\varepsilon$ is public and $A$ is hidden. Exact $Av$ is available for every $v\in\mathbb{R}^n$, and exact $A^{\mathsf T}u$ for every $u\in\mathbb{R}^m$. The two directions are charged separately.

Output

Return $P\in\mathbb{R}^{n\times n}$ satisfying $P=P^{\mathsf T}=P^2$ and $\operatorname{rank}(P)=k$, or an orthonormal basis for that projector. Neither $AP$ nor an error certificate is required.

Loss or accuracy criterion

For finite $p$, use $\|M\|_{S_p}=(\sum_i\sigma_i(M)^p)^{1/p}$; $p=\infty$ gives the spectral norm. Define $\operatorname{OPT}_{p,k}=\min_{\operatorname{rank}(B)\le k}\|A-B\|_{S_p}$.

Success means $\|A(I_n-P)\|_{S_p}\le(1+\varepsilon)\operatorname{OPT}_{p,k}$. Zero optimal residual requires exact recovery of the relevant row space. The unsquared criterion is retained.

Resource accounting

Retain the joint budget $(N_{\mathrm{r}},N_{\mathrm{l}})$, whose coordinates count single-vector calls to $Av$ and $A^{\mathsf T}u$, respectively. This setting explicitly uses the equal-weight scalarization $N=N_{\mathrm{r}}+N_{\mathrm{l}}$. Each column of a block is charged separately.

The budget bounds calls for every fixed input and every private seed. Reading public inputs, exact real arithmetic, storage, and postprocessing are free. One call applies the interface to one vector.

Algorithm views and success guarantees

Algorithms may use private randomness and choose query vectors adaptively from the declared domain using all previous responses. Queries and outputs may be arbitrary measurable functions of the transcript; no Krylov or linear-span restriction applies. Exact internal arithmetic, storage, and communication are free in this oracle model. A block query is charged by its number of columns.

The algorithm is selected using only public inputs. For every admissible input fixed before its private seed is generated, the success event has probability at least $2/3$ over that private randomness.

Budget convention
A fixed worst-case budget respected for every input and private seed.

Conditions
$2\le p\le C_{\mathrm{bridge}}\log(d_{\mathrm{min}})/\varepsilon$; $0<\varepsilon\le\varepsilon_0\le1$. The internal precision satisfies the BCW condition $p\le c_B\log(d_{\mathrm{min}})/\delta_B$.
Algorithm scope
Algorithms may use private randomness and choose query vectors adaptively from the declared domain using all previous responses. Queries and outputs may be arbitrary measurable functions of the transcript; no Krylov or linear-span restriction applies. Exact internal arithmetic, storage, and communication are free in this oracle model. A block query is charged by its number of columns.
Correspondence, constants and qualifications
Oracle correspondence
Exact $Av$ and $A^{\mathsf T}u$ are available for $v\in\mathbb R^n$ and $u\in\mathbb R^m$. Each column is charged separately. Block width and Krylov rounds do not replace total calls.
Guarantee conversion
Success probability is at least 2/3 for each fixed A. Retain the bound’s constant and accuracy windows for fixed and variable p.
Output rule
Output a right orthogonal projector $\widehat P$ of rank $k$ satisfying $\|A(I_n-\widehat P)\|_{S_p}\le(1+\varepsilon)\|A-A_k\|_{S_p}$. The input $A$ need not have low rank. If the optimal tail is zero, success requires exactly zero residual.
Resource conversion
Retain joint budget $(N_{\mathrm r},N_{\mathrm l})$ for single-vector $Av$ and $A^{\mathsf T}u$ calls, with the explicit equal-weight scalarization $N=N_{\mathrm r}+N_{\mathrm l}$. Charge each block column separately. The budget is a worst-case cap for every input and private seed, not an expected count. Reading public inputs and internal exact-real arithmetic, storage, and postprocessing are uncharged; query complexity is not runtime or bit complexity.
Constants
The constant $C$ is uniform in $m,n,k,p,\epsilon$. The quantities $c_B,C_{\mathrm{bridge}},\alpha_B$ are fixed universal proof constants.
Derivation
Let $\alpha_B=\min\{1/2,c_B/(2C_{\mathrm{bridge}})\}$ and run BCW with internal tolerance $\delta_B=\alpha_B\varepsilon$. If $p\varepsilon\le C_{\mathrm{bridge}}\log d_{\mathrm{min}}$, then $p\le c_B\log(d_{\mathrm{min}})/\delta_B$, while $\delta_B\le\varepsilon/2<1$. The source residual guarantee $(1+\delta_B)$ therefore implies the target $(1+\varepsilon)$ guarantee. Substituting $\delta_B$ into the query bound gives $N\le Ck\log(2d_{\mathrm{min}}/\varepsilon)[p^{1/6}\varepsilon^{-1/3}+\sqrt p]$. Since $\alpha_B$ is fixed in advance, the constants are uniform in varying p. When $m<n$, run the algorithm on $A^{\mathsf T}$ and include at most k additional $A^{\mathsf T}U$ calls to form the right projector. The resulting right subspace may be enlarged to rank k, which can only decrease the residual.
Branch condition
Assume $2\le p\le C_{\mathrm{bridge}}\log(d_{\mathrm{min}})/\varepsilon$, $0<\varepsilon\le\varepsilon_0$, and $1\le k<d_{\mathrm{min}}$. The universal constant $C_{\mathrm{bridge}}>0$ joins the two upper-bound branches.

Logarithmic factors

Derivation
Run the Musco-Musco block Krylov algorithm at internal spectral tolerance $\eta=\varepsilon/4$. The iteration count is $$ O\bigl(\varepsilon^{-1/2}\log(2d_{\mathrm{min}}/\varepsilon)\bigr). $$ Charging each column separately and including the output conversion gives $$ N\le Ck\varepsilon^{-1/2}\log(2d_{\mathrm{min}}/\varepsilon). $$ This branch requires $p\ge C_{\mathrm{bridge}}\log(d_{\mathrm{min}})/\varepsilon$, hence $d_{\mathrm{min}}^{1/p}\le1+\varepsilon/4$. Using $\operatorname{rank}(A(I_n-P))\le d_{\mathrm{min}}$ yields $$ \begin{aligned} \|A(I_n-P)\|_{S_p} &\le(1+\varepsilon/4)^2\operatorname{OPT}_{\infty,k}\\ &\le(1+\varepsilon)\operatorname{OPT}_{p,k}. \end{aligned} $$
Branch condition
Assume $C_{\mathrm{bridge}}\log(d_{\mathrm{min}})/\varepsilon\le p<\infty$, $0<\varepsilon\le\varepsilon_0$, and $1\le k<d_{\mathrm{min}}$, together with the unified comparison condition $p\ge2$.

Correspondence, constants and qualifications
Oracle correspondence
Exact $Av$ and $A^{\mathsf T}u$ are available for $v\in\mathbb R^n$ and $u\in\mathbb R^m$. Each column is charged separately. Block width and Krylov rounds do not replace total calls.
Guarantee conversion
Success probability is at least 2/3 for each fixed A. Retain the bound’s constant and accuracy windows for fixed and variable p.
Output rule
Output a right orthogonal projector $\widehat P$ of rank $k$ satisfying $\|A(I_n-\widehat P)\|_{S_p}\le(1+\varepsilon)\|A-A_k\|_{S_p}$. The input $A$ need not have low rank. If the optimal tail is zero, success requires exactly zero residual.
Resource conversion
Retain joint budget $(N_{\mathrm r},N_{\mathrm l})$ for single-vector $Av$ and $A^{\mathsf T}u$ calls, with the explicit equal-weight scalarization $N=N_{\mathrm r}+N_{\mathrm l}$. Charge each block column separately. The budget is a worst-case cap for every input and private seed, not an expected count. Reading public inputs and internal exact-real arithmetic, storage, and postprocessing are uncharged; query complexity is not runtime or bit complexity.
Constants
Exactly min{m,n} standard basis queries suffice, with no hidden logarithmic or p dependence.
Derivation
Public dimensions select a complete reconstruction algorithm; an internal SVD returns the right rank-k projection.
Gap or comparison
The ratio is at most $O\!\left(\log\!\frac{2d_{\mathrm{min}}}{\varepsilon}\sqrt{\log(2d_{\mathrm{min}})}\right)$, hence also $O\!\left(\log^{3/2}\!\frac{2d_{\mathrm{min}}}{\varepsilon}\right)$. Universal constants are independent of every $p\ge2$ varying in this region.
Comparison argument
Compare the bound of each complete algorithm with reconstruction in $d_{\mathrm{min}}$ queries, where $d_{\mathrm{min}}=\min\{m,n\}$ corresponds to the source dimension notation $N$. Three cases cover the full declared region. If $p\varepsilon\le1$, then $\sqrt p\le p^{1/6}\varepsilon^{-1/3}$. If $1\le p\varepsilon\le C_{\mathrm{bridge}}\log d_{\mathrm{min}}$, both BCW terms are bounded by $\varepsilon^{-1/2}\operatorname{polylog}(d_{\mathrm{min}})$. If $p\ge C_{\mathrm{bridge}}\log(d_{\mathrm{min}})/\varepsilon$, the spectral-norm conversion applies. Constants depending on fixed $p$ remain explicit; the $\sqrt p$ term growing with $p$ is retained. After rescaling BCW's internal tolerance, the first case incurs $\log(2d_{\mathrm{min}}/\varepsilon)$, the second adds at most $\sqrt{C_{\mathrm{bridge}}\log d_{\mathrm{min}}}$, and the third uses the single-logarithm spectral bound. With $\Phi_{\mathrm{lr}}(p,\varepsilon)=\min\{p^{1/6}\varepsilon^{-1/3},\varepsilon^{-1/2}\}$, this gives $Q_{\mathrm{upper}}\le\min\{d_{\mathrm{min}},Ck\Phi_{\mathrm{lr}}(p,\varepsilon)\log(2d_{\mathrm{min}}/\varepsilon)\sqrt{\log(2d_{\mathrm{min}})}\}$. The minimum includes only applicable branches. BCW's parameter window is enforced using $\delta_B=\alpha_B\varepsilon$ with the stated rescaling constant; it cannot be dropped by silently changing hidden constants.

Since $d_{\mathrm{min}}\ge2$ and $\varepsilon\le\varepsilon_p\le1$, BCW's applicability condition $p\le c_B\log(d_{\mathrm{min}})/\delta_{\mathrm{low}}$ holds. The factors $p^{1/6}$ and $\sqrt p$ in its total query bound can be absorbed into constants depending on fixed p, giving $N\le C_p k\varepsilon^{-1/3}\log(2d_{\mathrm{min}}/\varepsilon)$.
